II. Squaring the residuals ensures that offsetting positive and negative errors are not treated as acceptable as zero errors, and that large errors are penalized heavily relative to small ones.

III. Each residual is measured horizontally on the scatter plot, as the gap between the actual and the predicted change in the government security yield.

**How least squares estimates beta**

Stem in one line: four documentation statements on how the INR beta is estimated; which are accurate?

**Concept and theory**

GARP §11.1 sets out the estimation step by step. Given estimates $\hat{\alpha}$ and $\hat{\beta}$, the predicted change in the hedged yield is $\widehat{\Delta y^{P}_{t}}$ = $\hat{\alpha}$ + $\hat{\beta}$ ∆$y^{H}_{t}$ (Eq. 11.2). The realized residual is actual minus predicted, $\hat{\epsilon}_{t}$ = ∆$y^{P}_{t} - \widehat{\Delta y^{P}_{t}}$ (Eq. 11.3, 11.4); on a scatter plot it is the vertical line from the data point to the regression line, in the units of the dependent variable. loText: Calculate the face value of an offsetting position needed to carry out a regression hedge.
question:
A portfolio manager at a US credit hedge fund has sold short USD 45 million face amount of a 10-year industrial corporate bond and will hedge its interest rate risk with the 10-year US Treasury note in a single-variable regression hedge. The fund’s risk system reports:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| DV01 of the short corporate position (whole position) | USD 36,540 per bp |
| DV01 of the Treasury note (per 100 face) | 0.0868 |
| Yield of the corporate bond | 5.48% |
| Slope from regressing ∆$y$ corporate on ∆$y$ Treasury | 1.12 |
| R-squared of that regression | 65% |

Which of the following describes the regression hedge?

*Conventions for this paper:* Unless stated otherwise, DV01s are yield-based and quoted per 100 of face amount, yield changes are in basis points, and a regression of “∆$y$ of X on ∆$y$ of Y” has X as the dependent variable.

options.A: Sell USD 47.15 million face amount of the Treasury note
options.B: Buy USD 47.15 million face amount of the Treasury note
options.C: Buy USD 42.10 million face amount of the Treasury note
options.D: Buy USD 37.59 million face amount of the Treasury note

solution:
**Hedging a short corporate position from its dollar DV01**

Stem in one line: short USD 45 million corporate, position DV01 USD 36,540 per bp, Treasury DV01 0.0868 per 100, slope 1.12; describe the hedge.

**Concept and theory**

Eq. (11.7) is a statement about dollar DV01s: the hedge’s dollar DV01 must equal $\hat{\beta}$ times the position’s dollar DV01, with the opposite sign. When the risk system gives the position’s DV01 in currency for the whole position, there is no need for the per-100 DV01 of the hedged bond:

$F_{h}$ = $- \frac{\hat{\beta} \times F_{p} \text{DV01}_{p}/100}{\text{DV01}_{h}/100} .$

loText: Calculate the face value of multiple offsetting swap positions needed to carry out a two-variable regression hedge.
question:
A derivatives trader at an investment bank is considering how to hedge a relatively illiquid 7-year USD interest-rate swap the bank just entered into as the fixed-rate payer. The trader recognizes that any profit resulting from the bid-ask spread may be lost if the trade is hedged with another illiquid 7-year swap and considers using the more liquid 5-year and 10-year USD interest-rate swaps as a hedge. To evaluate this possible hedge, the trader runs a two-variable regression model using changes in the 5-year and 10-year swap rates to explain changes in the 7-year swap rate. The regression model, regression results, and information about the swaps are given below:

Δyt7 = α + β5Δyt5 + β10Δyt10 + εt

|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
| Number of observations | 1255 |  |
| R-squared | 98.1% |  |
| Standard error | 0.12 |  |
| Regression coefficients | Value | Standard error |
| Constant (α) | 0.0012 | 0.0030 |
| Change in 5-year swap rate (β5) | 0.2471 | 0.0025 |
| Change in 10-year swap rate (β10) | 0.6536 | 0.0027 |

|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
| Swap tenor | Swap fixed rate | DV01 |
| 5-year | 2.591% | 0.061 |
| 7-year | 2.492% | 0.084 |
| 10-year | 2.475% | 0.115 |

What are the correct notional amounts of 5-year and 10-year swaps needed to hedge a USD 100 million notional amount of 7-year swaps?

options.A: USD 23.76 million of 5-year swaps, and USD 65.81 million of 10-year swaps
options.B: USD 24.71 million of 5-year swaps, and USD 65.36 million of 10-year swaps
options.C: USD 34.03 million of 5-year swaps, and USD 47.74 million of 10-year swaps
options.D: USD 68.85 million of 5-year swaps, and USD 36.52 million of 10-year swaps

solution:
**Concept**

A two-variable regression hedge. The regression tells how much the 7-year rate moves for a move in each hedging rate ($\beta_{5}$, $\beta_{10}$). Each hedge notional then has to offset that sensitivity in DV01 terms: $F_{k} = -F_{7} \times\frac{\text{DV01}_{7}}{\text{DV01}_{k}} \times\beta_{k}$.

**Working**

$$F_{5} = -100 \times\frac{0.084}{0.061} \times0.2471 = -34.03 F_{10} = -100 \times\frac{0.084}{0.115} \times0.6536 = -47.74$$

The bank pays fixed on the 7-year swap, so it receives fixed on USD 34.03 million of 5-year swaps and USD 47.74 million of 10-year swaps.

**Exam trap.** Three ingredients, and each distractor leaves one out: the betas (D), the DV01 ratio (B), or uses swap rates in place of DV01s (A). The constant $\alpha$ and the standard errors are not needed.

loText: Describe principal component analysis and explain how it is applied to constructing a hedging portfolio.
question:
The manager of the fixed-income desk of an investment bank is examining the current term structure of swap rates and believes that the 5-year swap rate is too low relative to the 2-year and 10-year swap rates. The manager asks a risk analyst to design a hedged butterfly trade in which the bank is the payer in a 5-year swap contract and the receiver in 2-year and 10-year swap contracts.

The analyst decides to perform a principal components analysis (PCA) of the term structure of swap rates and use the results of the PCA to construct the butterfly trade. The principal components (PCs) identified as having the greatest impact are the level, the slope, and the short rate. The results of the PCA, stated as the change in bps in the swap rates due to a 1 standard deviation increase in the PC, are given in the table below:

|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
| Term (years) | Level PC | Slope PC | Short Rate PC |
| 1 | 3.25 | -2.51 | 1.27 |
| 2 | 5.06 | -2.93 | 0.44 |
| 5 | 5.97 | -1.28 | -0.36 |
| 10 | 5.43 | 0.02 | -0.18 |
| 20 | 4.84 | 0.64 | 0.25 |

The analyst also notes that these three PCs explain over 99.5% of the variability in the swap rates, with the level PC having the greatest impact, the slope PC having a smaller impact, and the short rate PC only having an impact on very short-term swap rates.

To construct the hedged butterfly position, the analyst collects the current swap rates and DV01s of the 2-year, 5-year, and 10-year swaps, shown in the table below:

|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
| Term (years) | Swap rate | DV01 |
| 2 | 2.992% | 0.0285 |
| 5 | 2.551% | 0.0496 |
| 10 | 2.454% | 0.0731 |

After receiving this information from the analyst, the manager instructs the analyst to construct a butterfly position with a notional amount of EUR 100 million in the 5-year swap in such a way that exposures to the level and slope PCs are neutralized. What notional amounts of the 2-year swap and the 10-year swap should be included in the butterfly and what are the risk weights of the two swaps relative to the DV01 of the 5-year swap?

|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Notional of | Notional of |  |  |  |
| 2-year swap | 10-year swap | Risk weight of | Risk weight of |  |
| Choice | (EUR million) | (EUR million) | 2-year swap | 10-year swap |
| A | 23.15 million | 76.85 million | 39.1% | 60.9% |
| B | 46.68 million | 53.32 million | 44.2% | 68.8% |
| C | 46.68 million | 76.85 million | 44.2% | 68.8% |
| D | 46.68 million | 76.85 million | 39.1% | 60.9% |
solution:
**Concept**

A PCA butterfly hedge. Each principal component moves every swap rate by a known number of basis points. The P&L exposure of a swap to a PC is notional × DV01 × (bp move of that tenor). Choose the two wing notionals so that the exposures to the level PC and to the slope PC both net to zero against the 5-year body.

**Working**

Let $a = F_{2} \times0.0285$ and $b = F_{10} \times0.0731$ be the DV01 exposures of the two wings (per 100 of notional). The body has 100 × 0.0496 = 4.96.

**Level PC neutral:** $5.06 a + 5.43 b = 4.96 \times5.97 = 29.611$

**Slope PC neutral:** $-2.93 a + 0.02 b = 4.96 \times(-1.28) = -6.349$

**Solve.** From the slope equation $a = (6.349 + 0.02 b)/2.93$. Substituting into the level equation gives $5.4645 b = 18.647$, so $b = 3.412$ and $a = 2.190$.
